To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
- The D3-D7 system in a magnetic background field exhibits chiral symmetry breaking.

• The D3-D7 holographic model can be extended to include constant electric and magnetic fields, • Holographic magnetic fields lead to spontaneous chiral symmetry breakdown, • Holography allows for the introduction of N=2 supersymmetry breaking via a Fayet-Iliopolous term, • The N=2 supersymmetric Fayet-Iliopoulis term is dual to a particular Kalb-Rammon mode, • Matrix models can be extended to cosmologically expanding backgrounds
we have found holographic duals for electric and magnetic background-fields in the D3/D7 system and that we have shown the emergence of space time in matrix models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of holography as an important aspect of quantum gravity.
the holographic reformulation of strongly coupled gauge theories in the presence of external fields and with the holographic formulation of cosmology.
the study of holographic models, i..e. theories describing higher dimensional gravitational physics in terms of lower dimensional models without gravitation, and vice versa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
holography is an important tool to study strongly coupled quantum field theories and quantum gravity.

holography provides a powerful tool in the investigation of strongly coupled gauge theories, which can be used to address a variety of problems, such as the physics of quark-gluon plasmas, the physics of strongly coupled condensed matter systems or the physics of black hole horizons.
this thesis has contributed to a better understanding of holography, both in the context of strongly coupled gauge theories and in the context of quantum gravity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the introduction of external fields in the D 3 -D 7 model leads to interesting and new phenomena, and that the introduction of a time-dependent background in matrix models can be interpreted in a semiclassical way.
the holographic dual of a nonabelian field theory in a background with constant electric or magnetic field is a non-abelian field theory on a curved background.
the holographic dual of a nontrivial time dependence of the scale factor is the introduction of a time dependent potential for the matrix model degrees of freedom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
holographic dualities provide an efficient way to study the effects of external fields in gauge theories, and that the holographic approach can be extended to the study of time dependent backgrounds.

holographic techniques are a useful tool in the study of strongly coupled gauge dynamics, and can be used to gain insight into the physics of strongly coupled quark matter in the presence of external fields.
the D3-DN models are a rich playground for studying holographic models in external fields and in time dependent backgrounds.
